thread:
alex p: Heads up — I prototyped an allocator boundary sketch for tenant-aware demotion vs eviction. Wanted quick feedback before I write an RFC.

lina w: cool — what's the main abstraction? is it "resident vs soft-resident"?

alex p: yeah, something like that. Two calls from runtime: `ensure_resident(range)` and `demote_hint(range, reason)`. The former pins pages, the latter marks we can drop to host without losing correctness.

praveen r: important question: who owns the fallback policy? allocator or higher-level scheduler? feels like we need a clean split so runtime doesn't encode tenant fairness.

alex p: my thought — allocator exposes primitives (pin/demote/async_migrate) and exposes telemetry hooks. Scheduler makes admission decisions and calls primitives. keeps policy out of allocator.

morgan: that sounds sane. how do we surface fragmentation accounting? owners need to know when demote will cause lots of holes -> compaction triggers.

alex p: adding a lightweight `fragmentation_score(range)` in the API. returns a coarse bucket: low/med/high. Not perfect but enough for scheduling heuristics.

praveen r: I worry about chattiness. Calls per-infer should be tiny. maybe batch hints: `hint_batch([range...])` and allow coalescing.

alex p: good point — will design the shim to accept batches; runtime already batches kv-cache evicts.

lina w: what about the demote path latency? previous offload experiments showed spike on p95 for small-batch inferences when demote happened mid-request.

alex p: plan is `demote_hint` to be purely metadata; actual async_migrate(worker) does the heavy lifting. If an inference needs the data, `ensure_resident` will check for in-flight migrations and either wait or trigger a fast path (recompute or fall back to smaller model).

morgan: do we need a QoS-level: `priority_pin(range, ttl)`? for canary/latency-sensitive tenants.

praveen r: yes. But TTL semantics need to be clear. We had leaks before where pins were never released. ensure a finalizer / lease expiry in allocator.

alex p: agree. pins are leases: `pin(range, owner, ttl)` -> allocator returns lease_id. runtime must call `release(lease_id)` or wait for automatic expiry. we'll expose metrics for leaked leases.

eviction-bot: perf: demote-background-worker throughput at 60k pages/s on staging; p95 latency impact +18% when compaction kicked in. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

lina w: that's useful. maybe compaction should be rate-limited and coordinated with scheduler (only compact when global spare GPU memory > X).

morgan: also add a cost-estimate field: `migrate_cost(range)` approximate milliseconds and bytes. scheduler can use it to prefer recompute vs migrate.

alex p: nice idea. we'll add a coarse `cost_hint` to the fragmentation API.

praveen r: one more: API stability. we should avoid exposing internal slab details. keep ranges opaque (tokenized ids) and provide helpers to map model KV keys -> ranges.

alex p: done. no slab internals in public surface. only opaque range ids and metrics.

lina w: can you paste the minimal proto/IDL for the shim? then I can sketch scheduler integration.

alex p: sure:```\n// pseudo\nmessage PinRequest { repeated RangeId ranges = 1; string owner = 2; u32 ttl_ms = 3; }\nmessage DemoteHint { repeated RangeId ranges = 1; string reason = 2; }\nmessage Fragmentation { RangeId range = 1; string bucket = 2; uint64 cost_hint_ms = 3; }\n```\n
morgan: perfect. let's iterate in RFC. can we run a short canary on a single shard with pinned leases and observe tail?

alex p: planning that for next week. thanks all — I'll draft RFC with these primitives + telemetry and include the `hint_batch` and `lease` semantics.

lina w: thanks alex. will put scheduler impacts section in the RFC once you send the draft.

praveen r: ping me on the draft, I'll review the ownership boundaries.

alex p: will do. end thread.
